title: Grateful Dead Live at Newcastle City Hall on 1972-04-11
lineage: MR(recorded by Rex Jackson)>R(JG)>R(WB) Maxell UD XL reel tape @ 3 3/4 ips>Apogee Mini Me(24/96)>Apogee Mini DAC(monitoring)>LYNX ONE soundcard>Wavelab 5.0(dithered to 20/44)>CD

ai_review.summary: High‑energy Europe ’72 Newcastle show captured from a soundboard; stellar jams (The Other One’s “Feeling Groovy”, Truckin’, China/Rider) shine despite some hiss and occasional EQ needs.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised as one of the cream‑of‑the‑crop shows from Europe ’72, with the second set delivering a smoking The Other One jam, tight Truckin', soaring China/Rider and an inspired Looks Like Rain featuring pedal steel. The soundboard source is cleaner than many bootlegs but still carries noticeable hiss that benefits from EQ, yet listeners find it more than listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (12+) award 4‑5 stars and highlight exceptional musical moments; recording quality is mixed but generally acceptable, yielding an overall rating in the good‑to‑great range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeable tape hiss and occasional need for EQ; some reviewers call it “hissy” or “muddy,” but the master source is an improvement over older transfers and remains listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as unspectacular, but the second set erupts with a loose‑yet‑well‑jammed Truckin' leading into an extraordinary Other One suite; overall pacing builds to a high‑energy climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring vocals, explosive guitar work, and especially his pedal‑steel on Looks Like Rain; noted for the powerful “YEAH” shout at the end of I Know You Rider.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for a jazzy, bass‑themed movement within The Other One and praised for his singing on later songs.
band_member_comments.Bob: Acknowledged for solid rhythm guitar (some reviewers note past lyrical flubs but overall high standard) and energetic contributions to Truckin' and other jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s duet with Jerry during the post‑Truckin’ jam, gorgeous solo passages, and counterpoint work praised; noted for beautiful solos throughout.
